description: Zeek logs (zeek/<case>/<capture>/<log>.json): evidence time from ts (ISO8601 or epoch), event.dataset from the log name, labels.case/labels.item from the path, ECS endpoint copies from the conn 4-tuple, network.bytes on conn records. Native Zeek fields stay in place, except the ones whose names collide with an ECS object or across Zeek logs: files/weird `source` (a string) → zeek.log_source, ocsp/pe `id` (a file id string, where every other log has the id.orig_h/... tuple) → zeek.file_id, and `cmd` — a {name,key,value} record in redis, a string in mysql — split to zeek.redis_cmd / zeek.mysql_cmd so the bare name never has to be both. http.log and websocket.log carry a top-level Host header that libbeat would clobber, so Filebeat ships them nested under zeek_http / zeek_websocket (see filebeat.yml); the hoist below lifts their columns back to the root and moves the Host header to url.domain. (Bare per-protocol names the Malcolm dashboards read, like ftp/postgresql `user` or smtp `tls`, stay in place: logs-dxdfir@zeek is composed only into the zeek stream, so they do not clash with the ECS user / Suricata tls objects other streams carry.)

script.description: http.log and websocket.log carry a top-level `host` (the Host header) that libbeat clobbers with its own host object on the main input, so Filebeat ships them nested under zeek_http / zeek_websocket (filebeat.yml) with their dotted column names intact: hoist every column to the root, expanding id.orig_h-style names into objects, and move the Host header to url.domain
script.if: ctx.zeek_http instanceof Map || ctx.zeek_websocket instanceof Map
script.source: for (String w : new String[]{'zeek_http', 'zeek_websocket'}) { if (!(ctx[w] instanceof Map)) { continue; } Map m = (Map) ctx.remove(w); for (e in m.entrySet()) { String k = e.getKey(); def v = e.getValue(); if (k == 'host') { if (!(ctx.url instanceof Map)) { ctx.url = [:]; } ctx.url.domain = v; continue; } String[] parts = k.splitOnToken('.'); Map cur = ctx; for (int i = 0; i < parts.length - 1; i++) { if (!(cur[parts[i]] instanceof Map)) { cur[parts[i]] = [:]; } cur = (Map) cur[parts[i]]; } cur[parts[parts.length - 1]] = v; } }

rename.description: ocsp.log/pe.log carry a STRING id (the Zeek file id of the analysed object); every other log's id is the orig_h/orig_p/resp_h/resp_p tuple, which the component template pins as an object
files.log/weird.log carry a native STRING source (e.g. HTTP) that collides with the ECS source object; move it aside before the endpoint copies
redis.log's cmd is a {name,key,value} record; mysql.log's cmd is a string, so in one stream the bare name cannot be both — move the redis record to zeek.redis_cmd
and mysql.log's string cmd to zeek.mysql_cmd, so bare cmd is renamed away entirely (no dashboard reads it) rather than carrying one protocol's value

grok.description: zeek/<case>/<capture>/<log>.json: the case and the capture the record came from

script.description: conn: network.bytes = orig_ip_bytes + resp_ip_bytes (the connection's IP-level total, what the dashboards sum)
script.source: long b = 0; if (ctx.orig_ip_bytes != null) { b += ((Number) ctx.orig_ip_bytes).longValue(); } if (ctx.resp_ip_bytes != null) { b += ((Number) ctx.resp_ip_bytes).longValue(); } if (ctx.network == null) { ctx.network = new HashMap(); } if (ctx.network.bytes == null) { ctx.network.bytes = b; }
